newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dasa wants clear signal for Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Dasa wants clear signal for Eurofighter.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) said on Saturday Bonn's recent support for the Eurofighter military aircraft was welcome but not enough to ensure further investment by the company.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he was confident Bonn would approve funding for the purchase of 180 aircraft from Dasa.
But Dasa wanted concrete support to come through this summer or it would drop out of the four-nation project, spokesman Andreas Breitsprecher told Reuters at the Paris airshow.
"We welcome Mr. Waigel's statement as positive, but we need a very strong signal, or we will have to end our participation," he said.

Dasa wanted to see Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition approve Eurofighter funding of 23 billion marks when it meets in July, Breitsprecher said. "That would make the future for us very clear," he said.
The company, a unit of carmaker Daimler-Benz AG, has said it was spending one million marks per day on the Eurofighter without any guarantee of orders from Bonn.
Britain and Spain have committed to buying the fighter, while Italy was still reviewing procurement.
The Eurofighter project includes British Aerospace Plc, Spain's state-owned Construcciones Aeronauticas SA and Alenia SpA of Italy's Fin Meccanica group.
